newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek premier slams new farmers' roadblock threat.
newsitem.headline: Greek premier slams new farmers' roadblock threat.

text.p: Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis on Friday rejected farmers' threats to resume a highway blockade to back demands for cheaper fuel, bigger state subsidies and an enhanced produce price support system..
"No government or society can tolerate a coercion of a small group which harms the rights of other citizens, their freedom and daily struggle for their income," Simitis told parliament.
Farmers' representatives said this week they would block national roads with tractors in early February unless their demands were met.
"We are warning the government 20 days ahead of time in order to avoid bringing tractors out in the streets," farmers' representative Yannis Patakis said this week.

A 25-day blockade in December paralysed road traffic and left thousands of trucks stranded. The farmers suspended their action for the Christmas and New year holidays but have vowed to resume the protest if their demands were not met.

From January 28, Thessaly farmers in central Greece will launch a series of demonstrations, mostly aimed at disrupting public services, to show the government they mean business ahead of a full-scale blockade, Patakis said.
"We will block public services, tax offices and toll booths in our area to prevent the state from collecting money," he said. The blockade of national roads again could start on February 4.
